name: switchback
description: Trail discovery, planning, and navigation — web + iOS. Built on OpenStreetMap.

scripts.typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.json && tsc -p e2e/tsconfig.json && npm run typecheck --workspace=@switchback/web && npm run typecheck --workspace=@switchback/mobile && npm run typecheck --workspace=@switchback/ingest-worker

//audit: npm audit reports GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (brace-expansion DoS) with no fix available: the patch landed only in 5.0.8, and eslint reaches it through minimatch@3, which calls the v1 default export that v5 removed — overriding to ^5.0.8 clears the audit and breaks `npm run lint` with `expand is not a function`. Left unpinned deliberately. Exposure is dev-only: brace-expansion is reached from eslint's config globbing over patterns from eslint.config.mjs and argv, never from user input, and eslint ships in no bundle. Revisit when @eslint/config-array moves to a patched minimatch.
//audit-uuid: uuid@7 (GHSA, bounds check in v3/v5/v6) reaches the tree through xcode@3 under @expo/config-plugins, and is the single root cause of every remaining advisory — the other nine entries npm lists are just the @expo/* packages that depend on it. Left alone: it is only executed by `expo prebuild`, against our own app.config.ts, and it appears in no shipped bundle — verified by exporting the iOS bundle and grepping it. Forcing uuid@11 there would swap the API out from under a package that has not been updated for it, trading a theoretical dev-time issue for a broken prebuild.
//overrides: postcss is scoped to `next` because that is the only place a bad copy comes from — Next pins it at exactly 8.4.31, three advisories behind (worst: arbitrary .map file disclosure via sourceMappingURL, fixed in 8.5.18). sharp is global and deliberately so. Next declares it `optional`, and an override that narrows an optional dependency out of its declared range does not upgrade it — npm decides it is unsatisfiable and, because it is optional, silently installs nothing. `next/image` then falls back to unoptimised output with no error, which is worse than the CVE. So sharp is a real dependency of apps/web at the fixed version (0.35.0 closed four libvips CVEs) and the global override keeps any nested copy from reappearing under it. That code path matters here: it is what resizes user-uploaded photos from R2 in Phase 3. next@16.2.12 is already the latest, so no upgrade resolves either of these.
//overrides-react: Both apps already pin 19.2.3, but pinning a dependency does not pin the tree: enough packages declare `react@^19.x` as a peer that npm hoists a newer patch alongside the pinned one, and a workspace ends up with two Reacts. React Native ships a renderer built against one exact React build and `expo-doctor` checks for that exact string, so the second copy is the one that breaks — at runtime, on the phone, with a confusing error. The override collapses the tree to one.
//engines: The floor is React Native 0.86's, copied verbatim rather than rounded down — with engine-strict=true in .npmrc, a mismatch is a failed install with a clear message instead of a Metro crash three commands later. Node 20.17 is below it, and Node 20 left maintenance in April 2026; Node 22 LTS or 24 is the answer, not 20.19.
